questions.stem: Which of the following tables exist within the GRC: Profiles application scope? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The GRC: Profiles application provides the foundational GRC table hierarchy: Document [sn_grc_document] (A) and Content [sn_grc_content] (D) are the base tables for policy/authority and citation/risk statement records; Indicator [sn_grc_indicator] (E) supports monitoring. Policy [sn_compliance_policy] (B) is in the Policy and Compliance scope. Risk [sn_risk_risk] (C) is in the Risk Management scope.

questions.stem: What are some characteristics of the ServiceNow Store? (Choose four.)

options.text: Some applications are certified by ServiceNow
All applications are certified by ServiceNow
Applications may be developed by ServiceNow Technology Partners
It houses both paid and free applications and integrations
Applications are built om the ServiceNow platform
Applications are certified by other developers

questions.explanation: Characteristics include all apps are certified by ServiceNow (B), apps may be developed by Technology Partners (C), it houses both paid and free apps and integrations (D), and all apps are built on the ServiceNow platform (E). A is excluded because "some" understates — ALL Store apps are certified before listing. F is incorrect — apps are certified by ServiceNow, not other developers.

questions.stem: Which role is not part of ServiceNow GRC?
questions.explanation: Risk Developer (B) is not a ServiceNow GRC role. The standard GRC Risk Management roles are Risk User [sn_risk.user] (A), Risk Manager [sn_risk.manager] (C), and Risk Reader [sn_risk.reader] (D), plus Risk Admin. There is no developer-level role in the GRC Risk Management module — all configuration is performed by admins.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true of a Risk Response task?

options.text: Only one Risk Response task can be related to a Risk at a time
Only users with the risk_manager role or higher can be assigned to a Risk Response task
The risk admin role is required to assign the Risk Response task
The Risk Response task is automatically progressed through the states using a workflow

questions.explanation: Risk Response tasks are automatically progressed through their states (Draft -> Work in Progress -> Awaiting Approval -> Closed) using a workflow (D). Multiple response tasks can relate to one risk (A is wrong). Any appropriate user can be assigned, not just risk_manager (B is wrong). No special admin role is required for assignment (C is wrong).

questions.stem: What table, along with the Policy table, is linked to the Control Objective table by a many-to-many relationship?
questions.explanation: The Citation [sn_compliance_citation] table (B) is linked to the Control Objective table via a many-to-many relationship, alongside Policy. Citations represent specific regulatory requirements that control objectives address. Entity Class (A), Authority Documents (C), and Risk Framework (D) do not have direct m2m relationships with Control Objectives.

questions.stem: Why would you create Entity classes?

options.text: To show relationships between tables or objects you are tracking that doesn’t otherwise exist anywhere in ServiceNow
To be assigned to risk statements, which generate risks for every Entity listed in the Entity Class
To be assigned to Control Objectives, which generate Controls for every Entity listed in the Entity class
To show relationships between Entities and Policies and map them directory to Citations

questions.explanation: Entity classes represent the types of things in the dependency model, enabling relationships between entity groups that do not otherwise exist natively in ServiceNow (A). The GRC: Workbench lets managers map dependency relationships between entity classes. Entity TYPES (not classes) are assigned to risk statements (B) and control objectives (C). D is incorrect — entity classes do not map policies to citations.

questions.stem: The Tablename.config:

options.text: Displays the configuration list view of the table in the browser tab
Displays the table in list view within the Content Frame
Displays the table in list view within a separate browser tab
Displays the configuration list view of the table in the Content Frame

questions.explanation: The Tablename.config URL pattern displays the configuration list view of the specified table within the Content Frame (D) — the main content area of the ServiceNow UI showing fields, business rules, ACLs, and other config elements. Tablename.list shows the data list view. The config URL does not open in a separate browser tab (C) and does not redirect to the browser tab title (A).

questions.stem: Which of the following extends from items?
questions.explanation: Control [sn_compliance_control] (B) extends the Item [sn_grc_item] table. Item is the base GRC table for core GRC objects. Citation (A) extends Content [sn_grc_content]. Issue (C) extends Task. Policy (D) extends Document [sn_grc_document]. Of the listed options, only Controls directly extend the Item table.

questions.stem: What happens when you assign an Entity Type to a Risk Statement?

options.text: An assessment will be automatically generated to test each Entity listed in the Entity Type
A risk assessment is created automatically for every Entity listed in the Entity Type
A risk is automatically generated for every Entity listed in the Entity Type
The Entity is now going to present a risk score and controls are going to be tied to it

questions.explanation: When an Entity Type is assigned to a Risk Statement, a Risk record is automatically generated for every Entity within that entity type (C). This mirrors how Control Objectives auto-generate Controls. An assessment (A, B) is not auto-generated at assignment time — assessments are triggered separately. D describes ongoing risk score visibility, not what is generated at assignment.

questions.stem: There is a direct relationship between Entity Class and Entity Type when:

options.text: They have the same Entity Types

questions.explanation: There is no direct relationship between Entity Class and Entity Type (B) — they serve different purposes and operate independently. Entity Classes are tags applied directly to Entity records for grouping. Entity Types are templates defining entity filter conditions, linked to Risk Statements and Control Objectives. No formal relationship table connects the two.

questions.stem: Which filter navigation syntax displays the table in list view within a separate browser tab?
questions.explanation: Standard ServiceNow navigation syntax. tablename.LIST (uppercase) opens the list view in a separate browser tab. tablename.list (lowercase) opens in the main content frame. tablename.config opens the configuration list view. This behaviour applies across all tables regardless of application module.

questions.stem: Jim is an Audit Manager. In addition to Audit Manager, which roles should be assigned to ensure he can manage the audit process as well as other GRC functions related to audit? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: sn_audit.manager covers audit-specific management but does not inherit broad GRC access. sn_grc.manager is required for managing risk and compliance GRC functions. sn_grc.user provides baseline GRC platform access. sn_audit.user (B) already contains sn_grc.user, making it redundant alongside C.

questions.stem: What table extends from Document Table?
questions.explanation: Risk Framework [sn_risk_framework] explicitly extends the Document [sn_grc_document] table and stores all risk frameworks. Risk [sn_risk_risk] extends Item; Risk Statement [sn_risk_definition] extends Content; Risk Response Tasks extend the platform Task table — none of the other options extend Document.

questions.stem: Which of the following are scoped applications related to the Risk and Compliance applications? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The four core scoped Risk and Compliance applications are GRC: Profiles/Entities (A), GRC: UCF Compliance (C), GRC: Policy and Compliance Management (D), and GRC: Risk Management (F). Performance Analytics (E) is an optional analytics add-on; Attestation Design (B) is not a primary standalone scoped application.

questions.stem: Which tables extend the Content (sn_grc_content) table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Citation [sn_compliance_citation] extends Content [sn_grc_content]. Policy Statement [sn_compliance_policy_statement] also extends Content. The Content table stores content-level items (citations, control objectives, risk statements) referenced within documents rather than being documents themselves.

questions.stem: All of the following are PARENT tables which exist within the GRC Entities application scope EXCEPT.
questions.explanation: The GRC Entities scope parent tables are Item [sn_grc_item] (base), Document [sn_grc_document] (extends Item), and Content [sn_grc_content] (extends Item). Indicator [sn_grc_indicator] belongs to the Common GRC Features scope and is not a parent table in the GRC Entities application scope.

questions.stem: Which table stored the links from Entity to Entity Types?
questions.explanation: The many-to-many relationship between Entities and Entity Types is stored in sn_grc_m2m_profile_profile_type, preserving the original Profile/Profile Type naming despite the UI renaming to Entity/Entity Type. The other options use application-specific prefixes (sn_compliance_, sn_risk_) for unrelated relationships.

questions.stem: Where does a policy get published to when it is approved?
questions.explanation: When a policy moves to the Published state, the system automatically generates a Knowledge Base article, making the policy available platform-wide. Knowledge Summit, ServiceNow Library, and Authoritative Records are not ServiceNow concepts used for policy publication.

questions.stem: What GRC module would you access in order to update Entity Types?
questions.explanation: The GRC application renamed Profile Types to Entity Types. The navigation path is All > Scoping > Entity Types. The Scoping module provides access to All Entities, Entity Types, Entity Classes, and Entity Tiers. Risk > Entities (A) points to the wrong module; Scoping > Profiles (B) uses old terminology; CMDB (D) is a separate platform application.

questions.stem: The ServiceNow Platform requires which external components in order to ingest data from other systems?

options.text: The platform includes an SDK template that allows developers to enhance it using Java
A messaging bus needs to be developed
The platform allows XML to be ingested, and it required developers to leverage XSLT to map it properly
The platform has Integration Service that allow users and developers to ingest data from a variety of sources

questions.explanation: ServiceNow IntegrationHub provides pre-built integration spokes and Flow Designer connectors enabling data ingestion from a wide variety of external systems. No external messaging bus is required. The platform natively supports REST, SOAP, JDBC, and many other protocols and is not limited to XML/XSLT transformation or Java SDK development.

questions.stem: You are working with your customer to determine necessary audit management workflow configurations. What should they know about the approval process for audit engagements? (Choose three.)

options.text: If the engagement is approved and there are remaining open tasks or issues, it automatically moves into the Follow Up state.
If the engagement is approved and there are no remaining open tasks or issues, it automatically moves into the Closed state.
If the engagement is rejected, it automatically moves back to the Fieldwork state.
If the engagement is approved and there are remaining open tasks or issues, it automatically moves into the Fieldwork state.
If the engagement is rejected, it automatically moves into the Scope state.

questions.explanation: Three explicit outcomes: approved + open tasks/issues -> Follow Up (A); approved + no open items -> Closed (B); rejected -> reverts to Fieldwork (C). Options D (Fieldwork on approval) and E (Scope on rejection) are incorrect — those states are not triggered by the approval or rejection action.

questions.stem: Which GRC application would you use to manage internal or external consultancy processes that aim to prove the effectiveness of controls?
questions.explanation: Audit Management automates internal audit team workflows to prove the effectiveness of controls through structured engagements. It is designed for both internal and external audit consultancy processes, using risk and compliance data to scope, plan, and prioritise control testing activities.

questions.stem: What are the Risk Scoring methods available in ServiceNow? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The two scoring methods are Quantitative (numerical, e.g. ALE = SLE x ARO) and Qualitative (rating scales). Inherent (C) and Residual (D) are score types representing risk before and after mitigation, not scoring methods. Calculated (E) is a monitoring metric derived from failure factors.

questions.stem: The Risk thresholds in the Risk Criteria Matrix (default values) do not line up with company needs. What should you do?

options.text: Configure the Risk Criteria in ServiceNow
Identify Risk that will benefit from the default values
Demonstrate Risk scoring scenarios using the default values
Use the default values to determine new company approach

questions.explanation: Risk criteria define scoring thresholds for likelihood and impact and are configurable at All > Risk > Administration. If defaults do not match company needs, the correct action is to configure the Risk Criteria in ServiceNow to reflect the organisation's risk appetite rather than adapt the organisation to the defaults.

questions.stem: Who can move a Policy into Review? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: From Draft state, the policy owner (D) is the primary actor initiating review. The policy approver (B) may also trigger this transition. Once in Review, the owner, owning group, and reviewers can modify the policy and either request approval or return it to Draft.

questions.stem: The Citation table is a child table of which parent?
questions.explanation: Citation [sn_compliance_citation] explicitly extends the Content [sn_grc_content] table. Authority Document (B) extends Document, not Content. Item (C) is the base table that Content itself extends. Document (D) is the parent of Policy and Authority Document, not Citation.

questions.stem: Control Failure Factor represents the impact of Control Failures on what score?
questions.explanation: Control Failure Factor = sum of failed controls weighting / total controls weighting. This feeds into the Calculated Risk Factor: (Indicator Failure Factor + Control Failure Factor) x Residual score. It does not directly alter the Inherent score (A), Residual score (B), or an undifferentiated Total (C).

questions.stem: Which one of the following is not a trigger for issue creation?

options.text: Manual issue created by any manager or admin role as well as by audit user
Risk assessment returns the inherent and residual risk impact as ‘Very High’
Attestation returns the result as ‘Not Implemented’
Control effectiveness is ‘Ineffective’ and the state of control test is ‘Closed Complete’

questions.explanation: Documented issue creation triggers: manual creation (A), indicator failure (B), attestation result = Not Implemented (D), and control effectiveness = Ineffective with state Closed Complete (E). A risk assessment returning Very High inherent or residual impact (C) is not listed as a trigger.

questions.stem: GRC Options in Interactive Filters are only available through which feature?
questions.explanation: GRC Interactive Filters in dashboards and reports are provided exclusively through Performance Analytics. The GRC Analytics and Reporting Solution on the ServiceNow Store uses Performance Analytics indicator data to enable interactive filtering of GRC metrics over time.

questions.stem: In which state can reviewers either send the Policy back to draft or forward it by requesting approval?
questions.explanation: In the Review state, the owner, owning group, and reviewers can modify the policy and may reject it (returns to Draft) or request approval (moves to Awaiting Approval). No other policy lifecycle state allows both of these transitions simultaneously.

questions.stem: The Risk Scoring values are entered on the Risk Statement. What records inherits the values from the Risk Statement?
questions.explanation: When a risk is generated from a risk statement, it inherits the default scoring values (Inherent/Residual SLE and ARO, Impact, Likelihood) defined on the Risk Statement. Risk Criteria Matrix (A) stores thresholds; Risk Framework (B) organises statements; Risk Response Issue (D) is a remediation task — none inherit scoring from the risk statement.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describe the risk management lifecycle process?

options.text: Access, Identify and Plan, Control, Review
Control, Review, Assess, Identify and Plan
Identify and Plan, Assess, Control, Review
Identify and Plan, Review, Assess, Control

questions.explanation: The ServiceNow risk management lifecycle follows four phases in order: Identify and Plan (scope and define risks), Assess (evaluate likelihood/impact), Control (respond and mitigate), Review (monitor and report). Options A, B, and D present incorrect orderings of these same phases.

questions.stem: When calculating compliance scores, what is true about the weighting of Controls? (Choose two.)

options.text: Controls are not weighted equally by default
The weight of the Control is set when the Control is created

questions.explanation: The Control Weight field defaults to 10 (C) and is set when the control is created (D). The weighted control average is only applied when the system property "Use weighted control average" is enabled; by default controls ARE equally weighted at 10 each. Option A is therefore false in the default configuration; option B is false since weight is editable.

questions.stem: Which role(s) has the capability to create Policies? Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Doc explicitly states that in the Draft state a compliance admin, compliance manager, or Compliance User [sn_compliance.user] (C) can create a new Policy record. The sn_compliance.user role includes write access to Policy records in Draft state.

questions.stem: The ‘Add to Update Set’ utility is available for download via:
questions.explanation: The "Add to Update Set" utility plugin is available for download from the ServiceNow Developer site (developer.servicenow.com) (A). It is not distributed through the ServiceNow Store (B), Community (C), or HI Support (D), which serve different purposes.

questions.stem: What are the four values leveraged for the Inherent and Residual Risk Score Types?
questions.explanation: The Risk Scoring form exposes four values used for both Inherent and Residual score types: Impact and Likelihood (qualitative) and SLE (Single-Loss Expectancy) and ARO (Annual Rate of Occurrence) (quantitative). ALE (A, B) is a derived value (SLE × ARO), not a direct scoring input. Score (C) is an output, not an input field.

questions.stem: What would you leverage in order to provide users with an alternate user experience to view policies, create policy exceptions, and search for controls?
questions.explanation: The GRC Service Portal (D) provides an alternate consumer-facing interface for business users to view policies, submit policy exceptions, and search for controls — without requiring access to the full ServiceNow UI. Help Desk Portal (A), Catalog Portal (B), and Access Portal (C) are not GRC-specific portal names.

questions.stem: What type of customers may you encounter? (Choose three.)

options.text: Organization recently acquired and had some bad audit findings (using ServiceNow GRC to help restart their process)
Organization with little to nothing in place already (implementing one or more core ServiceNow GRC applications)
Organization undergoing a full GRC transformation (implementing all three core ServiceNow GRC applications at once or in a phased approach)
Organization implementing ServiceNow GRC to help ease their Customer Service organization (using other tools to manage other processes)
Organization implementing ServiceNow GRC to help ease their Help Desk organization (using other tools to manage other processes)

questions.explanation: The three standard ServiceNow GRC customer archetypes are: organizations restarting after audit findings (A), greenfield implementations with nothing in place (B), and full GRC transformations across all three core apps (C). Options D and E describe organizations using GRC to support non-GRC functions while relying on other tools for GRC itself — these are not GRC-primary customer types.

questions.stem:
Possible regulations when Entity scoping for Healthcare:
(Choose two.)
questions.explanation: HITRUST (A) and HIPAA (C) are the primary healthcare-specific regulatory frameworks used for entity scoping in ServiceNow GRC healthcare deployments. FISMA (B) applies to US federal government systems. HETRUST (D) is not a real regulation.

questions.stem: For Control records, who can modify the Control in the Draft state?

options.text: Only the person assigned the Attestation

questions.explanation: The Control form states: "Draft — In this state, all compliance users can modify the control." This is the broadest modification permission in the control lifecycle. Subsequent states (Attest, Review, Monitor) restrict modification to specific roles.

questions.stem: Control indicators may be triggered or scheduled in which state?
questions.explanation: Control indicators are triggered or scheduled when the control is in the Monitor state (B). The Monitor state represents continuous automated oversight of a control after attestation is complete. Draft (E) and Attest (D) are pre-monitoring states; Review (C) is a transitional state; Retired (A) controls are inactive.

questions.stem: Which role reviews the risk response and moves the Risk record into the Monitor state at the appropriate time?
questions.explanation: The Risk Manager [sn_risk.manager] (A) is the role responsible for reviewing completed risk response tasks and transitioning the Risk record to Monitor state once the response strategy is in place. Risk User (B) participates in assessments; Risk Reader (C) is read-only; Risk Owner (D) manages the risk record but does not drive the state transition to Monitor.

questions.stem: Entity scoping is used for what?

options.text: Make sure that all of your Entities have the right visibility
Create and assign controls to the correct users
Create, assign, and manage controls and risks across an enterprise
Scope out the different users and roles that have access to the platform

questions.explanation: Entity scoping is used to create, assign, and manage controls and risks across the enterprise (C) — scoping determines which entities are subject to which controls and risks. Option A (visibility) is a consequence, not the purpose. Option B (assigning to users) is partial. Option D describes role/access management, not entity scoping.

questions.stem: The SOX content pack includes a series of policies, control, risks. How are all of these components linked together?
questions.explanation: When a content pack such as SOX is imported, all components (policies, controls, risks, audit plans) are automatically linked together by the import process (C). No manual linking (B) or mapping files (A) are required. Batch import (D) describes the mechanism but not the linking behaviour.

questions.stem:
UCF has a collection of what? Select all UCF terms.
(Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The UCF Common Controls Hub contains three primary content types mapped to ServiceNow GRC: Authority Documents (B), Citations (D), and Controls (E) — which transform into Control Objectives. Control Indicators (A) and Policies (C) are ServiceNow-internal constructs not provided as UCF content types.

questions.stem: As a customer reaches greater GRC maturity, what can we expect to see occurring across their organization? (Choose three.)

options.text: Single Risk and Control frameworks across enterprise available to all stakeholders
Reliance on spreadsheet management for risk reporting
Continuous real-time monitoring of control performance

questions.explanation: As GRC maturity increases, organizations develop unified risk and control frameworks across the enterprise (A) and continuous real-time monitoring of control performance through automation (C). Cross-functional automation (D) and unified frameworks are related, but the exam recognises A and C as the two primary maturity markers. Spreadsheet reliance (B) and reactive strategies (E) indicate low maturity.

questions.stem: Which scheduled jobs in the GRC: Profiles scope help manage the population of Entity records? (Choose two.)

options.text: GRC Entity and Risk Statement Data Collection

questions.explanation: Two scheduled jobs in the GRC: Profiles scope manage entity record population: GRC indicator nightly run (A), which collects supporting data for entity-linked indicators, and GRC Profile Generation (C), which scans entity filter conditions and creates entity records from matching source table records. Options B and D are not valid scheduled job names.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct statement about Risk Scoring formulas?
questions.explanation: The quantitative risk formula is SLE × ARO = ALE (A): Single-Loss Expectancy multiplied by Annual Rate of Occurrence equals Annual Loss Expectancy. This is the foundational quantitative risk formula. Options B and C invert the formula incorrectly. Option D (Impact × Urgency) conflates ITSM priority calculation with risk scoring.

questions.stem: For classic risk assessment, while a Risk is in the Assess state, reviewers can do which of the following? (Choose two.)

options.text: Answer the assessment, moving the Risk to Respond
Set the Risk back to Draft

questions.explanation: While a Risk is in the Assess state, reviewers can: answer the assessment which moves the Risk to Respond (A) if a response strategy exists, or set the Risk back to Draft (D) by cancelling the assessment. Setting to Monitor (B) happens after response completion. Deleting the Risk (C) is not an Assess-state action.

questions.stem: What is the condition that must exist to edit the factor guidance of a published risk assessment methodology (RAM)?

options.text: All assessment instance records are in the Monitor state
All assessment instance records are closed
All assessment instance records are deleted
States of the assessment instance records are irrelevant
All assessment instance records are canceled

questions.explanation: To edit factor guidance on a published RAM, the RAM must first be moved back to Draft state. This is only possible when no assessment instance records exist in Monitor or Closed state; moving to Draft automatically deletes any in-progress instances. The net condition is that all assessment instance records are deleted (C) before factor edits are possible.

questions.stem: Policies can be automatically published after which of the following occurs?

options.text: Related control objectives are marked active
Policy is approved by all approvers
Policy is approved by one approver

questions.explanation: In the Awaiting Approval state, approved policies automatically transition to the Published state. If no approvers are identified on the policy form, the state is skipped and the policy publishes without approval. Policies rejected in this state return to Review.

questions.stem: To allow other applications to request a policy exception, you must complete the integration registry form. In addition to providing the name of the registry entry, what additional information is needed to complete the form?

options.text: You must indicate the audience for requesting policy exceptions
You must indicate the intended Service Portal
You must indicate the policy exception target table
You must indicate the allowed policy acknowledgement campaigns

questions.explanation: To enable other applications to request policy exceptions, they must be registered in the Integration Registry. In addition to the registry entry name, you must specify the policy exception target table — the table from which exception requests will originate.

questions.stem: The overall goal of Entity Classes is to:

options.text: To enable reporting and to support advanced risk assessment
Show relationships between Entities and policies and map them directly to Citations
Associate Control Objectives and Risk Statements with Risks and Controls
To provide specific information about an Entity, such as who owns the Entity

questions.explanation: Entity Classes are used to categorise and tag entities at a conceptual level (e.g., by location, business unit, or criticality). This tagging enables reporting across entity groupings and supports advanced risk assessment by allowing risk scoring to be aggregated and compared across class-based segments of the entity population.

questions.stem: What is the minimum role required for creating a policy acknowledgement campaign?
questions.explanation: The Compliance Manager role description explicitly includes "Setting up a policy acknowledgement campaign" as a capability of that role, along with scoping controls, creating attestations, and monitoring compliance. This indicates sn_compliance.manager is the minimum role required.

questions.stem: Which of the following are the classic risk score types that ServiceNow tracks? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three classic risk score types tracked in ServiceNow are Inherent (before any mitigation), Residual (after all mitigation), and Calculated (derived from indicator and control failure factors). Operational (D) and Digital (E) are types of risk, not risk score categories.

questions.stem: What is the condition that must exist to edit the risk scoring logic of a published risk assessment methodology (RAM)?

options.text: All assessment instance records are closed
All assessment instance records are deleted or canceled
All assessment instance records are in the Monitor state
All assessment instance records are in the Draft state

questions.explanation: A RAM can only be moved back to the Draft state if there are no assessment instances. When an assessment instance is in the Monitor or Closed state, the RAM cannot be moved to Draft. Deleting or cancelling all instances removes them, satisfying this condition.

questions.stem: Which of the following extends from Document Table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Policy [sn_compliance_policy] explicitly extends the Document [sn_grc_document] table. Authority Document [sn_compliance_authority_document] also extends Document. Citation (A) extends Content; Control Objective (C) extends Content — neither extends Document.

questions.stem: What is the minimum role required to create a risk assessment methodology (RAM)?
questions.explanation: The setup checklist and RAM retirement procedure both require sn_risk.admin. The Risk Admin role contains reader, user, and manager roles and is responsible for creating and managing RAMs. No lesser role in the Risk Management application has this capability.

questions.stem: Which table stores the links from Policy to Control Objective?
questions.explanation: The many-to-many table managing relationships between policies and control objectives is sn_compliance_m2m_policy_policy_statement. Of the available options, C (sn_compliance_m2m_policy_statement) represents this relationship. Options A and B link policies to entity types/entities; D links statements to entity types.

questions.stem: What is a risk register?
questions.explanation: "The risk register is the central repository for all potential risks that could occur at any time, anywhere in the organization." A is wrong (risk register tracks identified risks, not unidentified). B and C describe the risk library (frameworks and statements), not the register.

questions.stem: Which feature would you use to track completion of certain tasks?
questions.explanation: Task SLAs are used to track task completion, with notifications sent at 50%, 75%, and upon breach of the due date. Related Lists (A) display data only. Workflow Editor (C) and Notifications (D) are configuration tools, not tracking mechanisms for task completion progress.

questions.stem: Which GRC application would you use to determine where the organization is the most vulnerable or has the most exposure?
questions.explanation: Risk Management is the GRC application designed to identify, assess, score, and respond to organisational risks. It surfaces where the organisation has the greatest exposure through risk registers, risk scoring matrices, and risk heatmaps. Audit Management (B) tests controls; Policy and Compliance (C) monitors control effectiveness; Vendor Risk (A) assesses third parties.

questions.stem: What are the terms for level of risk before and after any actions are taken? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Inherent risk (C) is the level of risk before any mitigation strategies are in place. Residual risk (E) is the level remaining after all mitigation strategies are applied. Operational (A) and Digital (B) are risk categories; Calculated (D) is a monitoring metric; Solutioned (F) is not a GRC term.

questions.stem: What types of tasks are specific to the Audit module? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Audit-specific task types are Activity, Interview, Walkthrough, and Control Test. The docs confirm "activity, interview, and walkthrough can be created in Scope state" and "control tests can be generated in Validate or Fieldwork state." Control Attestation (A) and Remediation (F) are not audit-specific task types.

questions.stem: What baseline criteria determine when notifications are triggered in relation to audit tasks? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Notifications are sent when an audit task is reassigned (C). A notification is also sent when the task reaches 75% of its planned duration. Expiration (A) is inferred as a likely trigger when the due date passes. Options B (50%) and D (due date change) are not explicitly listed as baseline notification triggers.

questions.stem: What minimum role is needed to bulk initiate risk assessments using the risk assessment scheduler?
questions.explanation: The Risk Admin [sn_risk.admin] role contains the reader, user, and manager roles. The risk assessment scheduler is a management-level function; sn_risk.manager is the minimum role sufficient for bulk initiating risk assessments, while sn_risk.admin encompasses management privileges.

questions.stem: Common controls from UCF import into which table in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: The "Default Control transform" maps data from the UCF Control staging table into the Control Objective table [sn_compliance_policy_statement]. UCF Controls become Control Objectives, not policies (A), policy exceptions (C), or authority documents (D).

questions.stem: An Entity can belong to one or multiple of which of the following?
questions.explanation: An entity type is a grouping of entities based on filtering criteria. An entity can be associated with one or multiple Entity Types, enabling flexible grouping for scoping and risk/control assignment. Information Objects (B), Departments (C), and Entity Classes (D) do not support a direct one-to-many entity membership model.

questions.stem: When reviewing the Control Objective Table form with your customer, what are the most common choice lists to be configured? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: On the Control Objective (Policy Statement) form, the most commonly configured choice lists are Classification (e.g., Internal/External), Category (grouping type), and Type (e.g., Preventive, Detective, Corrective). Reference (A) is a table reference field, not a choice list. Description (E) is a free-text field and not configurable as a choice list.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow roles can manually move a Control record into the Monitor state? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: In ServiceNow GRC, moving a Control record to the Monitor state (making it live and actively monitored) requires either the System Administrator role (B), which has platform-wide authority, or the Compliance Manager role (D), which governs the control lifecycle. Control Owner (A) has accountability but not the state-change privilege; Process Owner (C) is not a standard GRC role.

questions.stem: For classic risk assessment, what are the risk components that apply to the Qualitative method? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Qualitative Impact uses Impact (significance of risk) and Likelihood (probability of occurrence), scored by multiplying the two. SLE (A) and ARO (B) are components of the Quantitative (monetary) method, not the Qualitative method.

questions.stem: On which records is the entity a required field? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Entity is a required field on Risk (A) and Control (B) records, as these items must be scoped to a specific entity for assessment and monitoring. Policy (C) and Control Objective (D) are framework-level records not tied to a specific entity instance. Risk Statement (E) is a template, not entity-specific.

questions.stem: Entity Types are applied to which types of records? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Entity Types are applied to Risk Statements (A) to scope which entity types are subject to a risk, Control Objectives (D) to auto-generate controls per entity, and Policies (E) for policy acknowledgement scoping. Issues (B) and Risks/Controls (C/F) are generated records, not directly assigned Entity Types.

questions.stem: What new related list was added to the risk statement and entity records after migrating to advanced risk assessment?
questions.explanation: After migrating to Advanced Risk Assessment, the Aggregated Risk related list is added to Risk Statement and Entity records to show rolled-up scores across the risk statement and entity hierarchy. Classic risk individual scores no longer roll up once migration is complete.

questions.stem: What ensures that every time you create an Entity from a specific table, the Class of the Entity is set according to the rule?
questions.explanation: Entity class rules assign entity classes at the table level. Any new entity created from a specific source table automatically receives the entity class defined by the matching rule. Entity business rules (B), class assignment (C), and type rules (D) are not valid GRC configuration terms.

questions.stem: The consolidated assessment feature can be used on which of the following? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The consolidated assessment feature is available for Classic risk assessments (B) and Control attestations (D). It allows respondents to provide the same or different responses across a group. Control tests (A) and Issues (C) do not use the consolidated assessment feature.

questions.stem: Which table stores the links from the Entity Type to Risk Statement?
questions.explanation: The table sn_risk_m2m_risk_definition_profile_type (C) stores the many-to-many relationship between Entity Types (Profile Types) and Risk Statements (Risk Definitions). Option A has an incorrect table name prefix; B links Risk Frameworks to Entity Types; D does not exist.

questions.stem: For classic risk assessment, indicator failure factor represents the impact of risk indicator failures on what score?
questions.explanation: The Indicator Failure Factor (number of failed indicators / total indicators) represents the impact of indicator failures on the Inherent SLE score (D) in the classic risk model. This factor, combined with Control Failure Factor, feeds into the Calculated Risk Factor = (IFF + CFF) x Residual score.

questions.stem: Praveen is a Risk Manager. Why would he want to utilize Entity Types and Entities? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: A Risk Manager uses Entity Types and Entities to: monitor risk exposure across the enterprise (A), perform scoped risk assessments against specific entity populations (C), and participate in policy exception processes triggered by risk findings (D). Remediating vulnerabilities (B) is a Vulnerability Response function. Risk reporting (E) is a secondary benefit.

questions.stem: If you create a control manually and later decide to create them automatically, what will be the result?

options.text: ServiceNow will delete the manually created control
ServiceNow creates a duplicate control and notifies the control owner
ServiceNow creates a duplicate control without notifying the control owner
ServiceNow identifies the control and does not create a duplicate

questions.explanation: When auto-generation is enabled after a manual control already exists, ServiceNow creates a duplicate control for the same entity without notifying the control owner (C). It does not delete the manual control (A), and no notification is sent (ruling out B). Option D is incorrect — duplicates are created.

questions.stem: Which of the following records does not have a lifecycle?
questions.explanation: Control Objective (A) has no independent lifecycle — it inherits the state of its parent Policy and has no separate state machine. Policy (B) has Draft→Review→Awaiting Approval→Published→Retired; Policy Exception (C) has a request/approval workflow; Control (D) has Draft→Attest→Review→Monitor→Retired.

questions.stem: Which of the following relationship sets are considered a many-to-many relationship? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Control↔Risk (C) uses sn_risk_m2m_risk_control; Control Objective↔Entity Type (D) uses sn_compliance_m2m_statement_profile_type; Entity Type↔Entity (E) uses sn_grc_m2m_profile_profile_type. Entity Type↔Entity Class (A) is a reference field on Entity Type, not m2m. Indicator Template↔Entity Type (B) is also a reference relationship.

questions.stem: How can you get the SOX content pack?
questions.explanation: Content packs including SOX are available from the ServiceNow Store (A). They are not delivered via patch updates (B), platform upgrades (C), or Professional Services engagements (D).

questions.stem: Critical parts of a successful GRC implementation are understanding the customers current: (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Critical understanding of a customer's current state for GRC implementation includes their existing GRC processes (C), recent data breaches (D), and prior audit failures (E) — these define the gaps the solution must address. Regulatory requirements (A) and personas (B) are inputs to future-state design, not current-state assessment.

questions.stem: Which of the following are ServiceNow classic risk score types? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: ServiceNow classic risk has three score types: Inherent (C) — before mitigation; Residual (E) — after mitigation; and Calculated (B) — derived from Indicator Failure Factor and Control Failure Factor applied to the Residual score. Applied (A) and Generated (D) are not valid risk score types.

questions.stem: A control objective has been related to a risk statement and they've been scoped with the same entity type. What can we expect to occur?

options.text: Risks for this risk statement will be moved back into a Review state since there are new factors impacting risk likelihood.
A control for this control objective, with a matching entity, will be related to the registered risk for this risk statement as a mitigating control.
The control objective will be marked as compliant since it is mitigating the related risk statement.
Risk scores will automatically decrease for the risk statement's risks since there are now mitigating controls.

questions.explanation: When a control objective and risk statement share the same entity type, the platform automatically links generated controls to generated risks as mitigating controls (B), only where the control entity matches the risk entity. Risk states (A) are not reset; control compliance (C) is not auto-set; risk scores (D) do not automatically decrease.

questions.stem: Santa Clara Facility and Boston Facility are examples of what?
questions.explanation: Santa Clara Facility and Boston Facility are examples of Entity Classes (C) — conceptual tags applied to entities to group them by physical location. Entity classes represent the categorisation dimension (e.g. location-based facility tag) rather than the entity records themselves.

questions.stem: Which collection of tables extend the Item (sn_grc_item) table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Risk [sn_risk_risk] (A) and Control [sn_compliance_control] (D) both directly extend the Item [sn_grc_item] table. Citation (B) extends Content which extends Item. Policy (C) extends Document which extends Item. Both are indirect, not direct, Item extensions.

questions.stem: Who should be directly involved in GRC implementations? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Parties directly involved in a GRC implementation are ServiceNow platform experts (C), Business Analysts (D), Risk and compliance experts (E), and CMDB process owner (F) — all hands-on contributors. Board of directors (A) and Chief Executive (B) are executive sponsors who provide direction but are not directly involved in day-to-day implementation activities.

questions.stem: Which of the following are triggers for automatic creation of an issue? (Choose two.)

options.text: Indicator result is Failed or Not Passed
Control tests have been assigned but not tested

questions.explanation: Automatic issue creation is triggered by: attestation result of Not Implemented (A) which creates a Control Issue, and indicator result of Failed or Not Passed (B) which creates an Issue. Policy exception rejection (C) and unassigned control tests (D) do not automatically create issues.

questions.stem: Risk criteria typically include definitions of different levels of what? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Risk criteria define different levels of Impact (A) and Likelihood (B) using qualitative rating scales (e.g. Very Low to Very High). These scales are configured in Risk > Administration > Risk Criteria. Criticality (C), Importance (D), and Priority (E) are not standard risk criteria dimensions in ServiceNow GRC.

questions.stem: Which is not a type of key compliance indicator?
questions.explanation: The three method types for GRC indicators are Manual (task-based), Basic (filter condition), and Script (scripted). Reference and Performance Analytics are not standalone indicator types — Performance Analytics is a data source option within indicators, not a separate indicator type.

questions.stem: The Entity Type table has a many-to-many relationship with which tables? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Entity Type has a many-to-many relationship with Risk Statement via sn_risk_m2m_risk_definition_profile_type (A). Policy links to Entity Type via sn_compliance_m2m_policy_profile_type (B). Controls (C) are generated per entity from control objectives; Risk records (D) are generated per entity from risk statements — neither is a direct m2m with Entity Type.

questions.stem: Unified Compliance Framework (UCF) uses a slightly different nomenclature structure than ServiceNow. Common controls from UCF import into which table in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: The "Default Control transform" maps data from the UCF Control staging table directly into the Control Objective table [sn_compliance_policy_statement]. UCF Authority Documents map to Authority Document (B); UCF Citations map to Citation (D); Control (C) is a separate generated record.

questions.stem: What dependency modeling feature can be used in the Classic UI to build relationships between Entity Classes?
questions.explanation: The GRC Workbench is used in the Classic UI to create entity classes and build the organisational dependency model. Navigating to $grc_workbench.do opens the workbench, which provides links for Dependency Model, Entity Types, and Dependency Map. Dependency Model Builder (B), Data Model Designer (C), and GRC Tree Map (D) are not ServiceNow features.

questions.stem: The content table (sn_grcs_content) is a parent table of:
questions.explanation: Risk Statement [sn_risk_definition] explicitly extends the Content [sn_grc_content] table. Entity [sn_grc_profile] extends Item; Risk Framework [sn_risk_framework] extends Document; Risk [sn_risk_risk] extends Item. Content is the parent only of content-type records: citations, control objectives, and risk statements.

questions.stem: Which of the following roles can create a policy? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: "A compliance admin, compliance manager, or a compliance user can create a policy." Compliance User (B) and Compliance Manager (C) map directly to sn_compliance.user and sn_compliance.manager. Audit User (A) and Risk User (D) have no policy creation rights. Compliance Reader (E) is read-only.

questions.stem: Which filter navigation syntax displays the default form view of the Risk table in the Content Frame?
questions.explanation: tablename.form (lowercase) opens the default form view of the table within the main content frame. tablename.list (lowercase) opens the list view in the content frame. tablename.LIST (uppercase) opens the list in a separate tab. tablename.FORM (uppercase) is not a standard navigation syntax. sn_risk_risk.form is the correct format for the Risk table.

questions.stem: What three records need to be set-up when integrating with a provider RSS feed? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Setting up an RSS feed for regulatory change requires three records: a Feed Source record (A) defining the feed name and linking to the provider and connection; a Provider record (B) identifying the regulatory body; and a Connection and Credentials record (D) providing the HTTP connection details.

questions.stem: Which of the following are Policy Lifecycle states included in the ServiceNow baseline? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The baseline policy lifecycle states are Draft, Review, Awaiting Approval, Published, and Retired. Review (B) and Published (D) are both standard baseline states. Expired (A) is not a state — expired policies remain in Published state. Acknowledged (C) and Verified (E) are not policy lifecycle states.

questions.stem: Which of the following extends from Content Table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Citation [sn_compliance_citation] explicitly extends the Content [sn_grc_content] table. Control Objective [sn_compliance_policy_statement] also extends Content. Policy (B) extends Document, not Content. Authority Document (D) extends Document, not Content.

questions.stem: Which tables extend from the Task table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Risk Response Task [sn_risk_response_task] is documented as extending the platform Task table (B). Risk Event [sn_risk_advanced_event] also extends Task in the Advanced Risk module (D). Risk Framework (A) extends Document; Risk Statement (C) extends Content; Risk (E) extends Item — none of these extend Task.

questions.stem: What are some of the drivers for customers to get the GRC suite of applications? (Choose four.)

options.text: They would like automated customer service
They would like workflow driven processes

questions.explanation: efficiency (A) through automating manual GRC processes; integrated reporting (B) across risk, compliance, and audit; transparency (C) into risk and control posture; and workflow-driven processes (F) for structured task management. Automated customer service (D) and custom websites (E) are not GRC business drivers.

questions.stem: The Calculated Risk Score utilizes data from the Inherent and Residual Risk scores to determine an adjusted ALE and Score. What other data drives the adjustments?
questions.explanation: The Calculated Risk Score is derived from: (Indicator Failure Factor + Control Failure Factor) x Residual score. Both the Control Failure Factor and the Indicator Failure Factor drive the adjustments to the Calculated score. Audit Scores (A), Attestation Scores (B), and Configuration Test Scores (C) do not feed into this formula.

questions.stem: The advanced planning capability enables integration of Advanced Audit with PPM. If the advanced planning capability is selected when the audit plan is created, what extra related lists display on the engagement record in addition to the related lists displayed with basic planning? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: When advanced planning is enabled, three additional related lists appear on the engagement record: Time card (A), Resource plan (B), and Cost plan (D). Entities (C) appear in basic audit engagements. Milestones (E) are part of the basic planning feature, not exclusive to advanced planning.

questions.stem: Which of the following roles can create issues? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Issue creation requires at minimum a user-level role in the relevant GRC module. Compliance User (D), Audit User (E), and Risk Manager (F) all have create rights on issue records. Risk Reader (A) and Compliance Reader (B) are read-only roles. External Auditor (C) has limited read access and cannot create issues.

questions.stem: What would you use in order to accommodate a customer’s unique process around policy approvals? For example, each policy needs a second layer of approval.

options.text: Create a new field and create notifications
Add a new related list to keep track of who has already approved it and who hasn’t approved yet
Add a UI Action to track who the stakeholders are
Create a new workflow in the workflow editor

questions.explanation: In ServiceNow, customising the policy approval workflow (e.g., adding a second approval layer) requires creating or modifying a workflow in the Workflow Editor (or Flow Designer). Adding a field (A), a related list (B), or a UI Action (C) would only surface information — they cannot enforce a structured multi-step approval process. Workflow is the correct mechanism.

questions.stem: Which of the following are a part of the GRC: Advanced Risk scope? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Advanced Risk scope includes Risk Hierarchy (A) — parent/child risk statement structure — and Risk Assessment Methodologies (B) — the RAM framework. Risk Criteria Matrix (C) and Risk Framework (D) are classic GRC: Risk Management scope components, not Advanced Risk.

questions.stem: Where does one go to configure the Regulatory Change Management impact assessment template?

options.text: Impact Assessment Flow in Flow Designer

questions.explanation: Regulatory Change Management uses Risk Assessment Methodologies (RAMs) to configure and run impact assessments on regulatory changes. The impact assessment template is therefore configured in the Risk Assessment Methodologies module, consistent with how risk assessments are structured across GRC.

questions.stem: Service Level Agreements can be used for the which of the following? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: In ServiceNow GRC, SLAs can be applied to task-based records. Risk Issues (A) are task-derived records that support SLA tracking with notifications at 50%, 75%, and breach. Risk Response Tasks (D) extend the platform Task table and therefore also support SLAs. Risk (B), Risk Statement (C), and Risk Framework (E) are not task-based records and do not support SLAs.

questions.stem: Controls are generated from a Control Objective when what is applied to it?
questions.explanation: Controls are automatically generated when an Entity Type is associated with a Control Objective. Each entity belonging to that Entity Type receives a corresponding Control record. Applying a Policy (A), Citation (B), or Indicator Template (C) to a Control Objective does not trigger control generation.

questions.stem: In which state is the Policy once all approvals are received?
questions.explanation: "Approved policies transition to the Published state." Once all approvers have approved the policy in the Awaiting Approval state, it automatically moves to Published, where a Knowledge Base article is generated. The policy does not return to Review (A), Draft (C), or Retired (D) upon full approval.

questions.stem: Setting up entity classes is required when using which GRC features? (Choose two.)

options.text: Setting up an object-based risk assessment
Adding to the policy exception integration registry
Assessing the impact of a regulatory feed

questions.explanation: Entity classes are required for Advanced Risk assessments (E) where the entity hierarchy with class tags drives risk score rollup. Object-based risk assessments (A) also require entity classes to define scope objects. Classic risk (D), policy exception registry (B), and regulatory feeds (C) do not require entity classes.

questions.stem: Which GRC tables serve as primary parent tables for the GRC applications? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Three primary GRC parent tables are Content [sn_grc_content] (A), Item [sn_grc_item] (B), and Document [sn_grc_document] (E). Item is the base; Document and Content extend Item. Risk/Control extend Item; Policy extends Document; Citation/Risk Statement/Control Objective extend Content. Asset (C) and Task (D) are not GRC parent tables.

questions.stem: Annualized Loss Expectancy is a feature of which risk score method?
questions.explanation: Annualized Loss Expectancy (ALE = SLE x ARO) is exclusively a Quantitative (B) risk scoring calculation using monetary values. SLE is monetary impact; ARO is annual probability. ALE is not a Qualitative (C) measure — qualitative uses ordinal Impact x Likelihood scales. ALE applies to both Inherent (D) and Residual (A) scores but the method is Quantitative.

questions.stem: For a particular risk assessment methodology (RAM), the control effectiveness score is calculated based on an individual assessment of controls. What are options for control identification? (Choose three.)

options.text: Controls are identified from library and ad-hoc
Controls are identified from indicator results
Controls are identified from related issues

questions.explanation: When using individual control assessment in a RAM, control identification options are: from library and ad-hoc (A), from library only (C), or ad-hoc only (D). These are the three dropdown options in the RAM Control Identification field. Indicator results (B) and related issues (E) are not control identification options.

questions.stem: Within the Policy Acknowledgement module, what table does the Acknowledgement Instance table extend from?

options.text: Does not extend from a table

questions.explanation: The Policy Acknowledgement Instance table does not extend from any other GRC or platform table (C) — it is a standalone table in the Policy Acknowledgement module. It does not inherit from Task (A), Policy Acknowledgement Campaign (B), Policy (D), or Document (E).

questions.stem:
For advanced risk assessment, risk response can be handled in the following ways:
(Choose two.)

options.text: Skipped entirely based on attributes defined in the RAM
Must create a mitigation response task
Must create at least one risk response task

questions.explanation: In advanced risk, response handling options are: create multiple risk response tasks (A) — the RAM allows multiple tasks per risk — and skip response entirely (B) — if the RAM is configured to not require a response. C and D are wrong — there is no mandatory minimum number of risk response tasks.

questions.stem: What assessment types can be enabled when configuring a risk assessment methodology (RAM)? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: A RAM can enable three assessment types: Residual Assessment (C), Inherent Assessment (D), and Control Assessment (E). Operational (A), Application (B), and Project (F) are not valid RAM assessment type options in ServiceNow Advanced Risk configuration.

questions.stem: How does GRC: Policy and Compliance Management track compliance to Authority Documents?

options.text: Citations are mapped to entity-scoped controls, which are tested as compliant or non-compliant.
Authority Documents are mapped to individual policies, which are either marked compliant or non-compliant.
Authority Documents are mapped to control objectives and compliance is checked when controls are tested as compliant or non-compliant.
Citations are mapped to control objectives, and compliance is checked when controls are tested as compliant or non-compliant.

questions.explanation: The compliance chain is Authority Documents -> Citations -> Control Objectives -> Controls. Citations (from authority documents) are mapped to control objectives (D), and compliance is tracked when controls are tested compliant or non-compliant. A incorrectly scopes citations to entity controls; C incorrectly maps authority docs directly to control objectives.

questions.stem: What are some of the features of scoped applications for GRC? (Choose three.)

options.text: Requires an entitlement for all environments
All components have a namespace prefix for identification
Provides access to all global data
Ability to view all components from the sys_metadata table
Ability to restrict access to available data

questions.explanation: GRC scoped apps require entitlements for all environments (A), all components have namespace prefixes like sn_grc_, sn_risk_, sn_compliance_ (B), and restrict access to available data by scope (E). They do NOT provide access to all global data (C) — that is a misconception. D is incorrect — sys_metadata is scoped to their own application.

questions.stem: Which of the following tables exist within the GRC: Profiles application scope? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: GRC: Profiles scope (sn_grc_) contains: sn_grc_profile_type (A — Entity Type), sn_grc_indicator (B — Indicator), and sn_grc_profile_class (E — Entity Class). sn_grc_compliance_policy_statement (C) is in the compliance scope. sn_grc_risk_definition (D) is in the risk scope, not Profiles scope.

questions.stem: Who can move a Policy record from Review into the next state?
questions.explanation: The policy owner (D) can request approval and complete the workflow on the policy record. Moving from Review to Awaiting Approval is requesting approval — an action initiated by the policy owner. Reviewers (C) can edit in Review but cannot advance the workflow. The compliance manager (B) requests the initial move from Draft to Review.

questions.stem: Which table extends from the Content Table?
questions.explanation: Risk Statement [sn_risk_definition] (D) extends the Content [sn_grc_content] table — Content is the parent for citation-like framework records. Risk Record [sn_risk_risk] (A) extends Item, not Content. Risk Framework (B) extends Document. Risk Response Task (C) extends Task. Risk Statement is the Content-level definition record.

questions.stem: What happens when you assign an Entity Type to a Control Objective?

options.text: An assessment is automatically generated to test each Entity listed in the Entity Type
A policy is created automatically for every Entity listed in the Entity Type
A control is automatically generated for every Entity listed in the Entity Type
The Entity Type presents a compliance score and controls tied to it

questions.explanation: When an Entity Type is assigned to a Control Objective, ServiceNow automatically generates one control record for every entity within that entity type (C). This is the core auto-generation feature. No assessment (A), policy (B), or compliance score display (D) is auto-generated by this assignment.

questions.stem: What are some of the baseline tables commonly leveraged in Entity filters? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Baseline tables commonly used in Entity filters are Company [core_company] (A), Services [cmdb_ci_service] (B), and Location [cmn_location] (C). These CSDM tables represent the organizational scope for entity populations. Risk [sn_risk_risk] (D) and Audit Engagement [sn_audit_engagement] (E) are GRC output tables, not entity source/filter tables.

questions.stem: An external audit team needs to view all of your published policies and controls? Which role can you give the team members?
questions.explanation: sn_audit.external_auditor (C) is designed for external audit teams needing read-only access to view published policies, controls, and audit records. sn_audit_manager (A) and sn_compliance_user (B) are internal roles with write privileges. sn_risk_user (D) provides risk-specific access, not audit/policy views for external parties.

questions.stem: An Observation can also be commonly known as what during an audit?
questions.explanation: In audit terminology, an Observation is commonly called a Finding (D). Audit observations/findings are results of audit reviews, interviews, and analysis brought to the attention of audit supervisors. Evidence (A) supports a finding. Engagement (B) is the audit project. Problem (C) is an ITSM concept.

questions.stem: What mapping capability in the Classic UI allows customers to relate specific Entities to each other within an Entity Class?
questions.explanation: The GRC: Workbench Dependency Map (C), accessed at $grc_workbench.do in Classic UI, is the mapping capability for relating entities within entity classes and defining dependency relationships. Entity Class Mapper (A) and GRC Entity Mapper (D) do not exist as GRC tools. Entity Workbench (B) is not a standard GRC Classic UI feature.

questions.stem: Which feature of classic risk scoring is frequently configured by customers?
questions.explanation: The Risk Criteria Matrix (B) is the most frequently configured classic risk feature — it defines qualitative impact and likelihood rating scales, score thresholds, and color-coded risk appetite bands. ALE (A) is a less-used quantitative feature. Control Failure Factor (C) and Indicator Failure Factor (D) are auto-calculated, not manually configured by customers.

questions.stem: Which methods does ServiceNow support when migrating new policies? (Choose three.)

options.text: They can be imported from PDFs
They can be imported via an API
They can be copied from the UCF
They can be imported from Regulatory websites
They can be imported from existing spreadsheets

questions.explanation: ServiceNow supports three policy migration methods: via API (B), created manually in the UI (C), and imported from existing spreadsheets via import sets (F). PDFs (A) cannot be directly imported as policy records. UCF (D) is for authority documents/citations, not policies. Regulatory websites (E) are not a supported direct import source.

questions.stem: Which collection of tables extend the Document table?
questions.explanation: Document [sn_grc_document] is extended by Risk Framework [sn_risk_framework], Policy [sn_compliance_policy], and Authority Document [sn_compliance_authority_document] (C). Policy extends Document (confirmed ). Risk Statement, Control Objective, and Citation (D) all extend Content [sn_grc_content]. Risk and Control (A) extend Item [sn_grc_item].

questions.stem: Which of the following tables are within the GRC: Policy and Compliance Management application scope? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Authority Document [sn_compliance_authority_document] and Policy Exception [sn_compliance_policy_exception] are both installed as part of the GRC: Policy and Compliance Management application scope. Assessment (B) belongs to the platform Assessment module; Audit Task (D) belongs to GRC: Audit Management.

questions.stem: What content can be ingested into ServiceNow as a result of the UCF integration? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: UCF imports two types of content into ServiceNow: Authority Documents (C) via the Default Authority Document transform, and Citations (E) via the Default Citation Transform. Policies (A), Risks (B), and Issues (D) are not ingested from UCF — UCF Controls map to Control Objectives, not to those records.

questions.stem: Entity Types use Entity Filters to generate entitles based on which of the following?

options.text: Only GRC scoped tables in ServiceNow

questions.explanation: Entity Types use Entity Filters to generate Entity records from any table in ServiceNow, not restricted to GRC or core platform tables. This allows GRC entities to be based on CMDB CIs, HR positions, financial accounts, or records from any custom or third-party table installed on the instance.

questions.stem: A relationship between a registered risk and a control will be automatically generated when the control objective and risk statement have the same what?
questions.explanation: When a Risk Statement and a Control Objective are associated with the same Entity Type, the platform automatically generates a risk-to-control relationship for each entity belonging to that Entity Type. The shared Entity Type is what triggers the automatic linkage between the generated Risk and Control records.

questions.stem: What do you select when you create a new assessment scheduler record for initiating advanced risk assessments? (Choose two.)

options.text: Entities from the designated entity type
Entities from the designated entity classes

questions.explanation: When creating an assessment scheduler record for advanced risk assessments, you select a published Risk Assessment Methodology (B) and entities based on the designated entity classes (D) associated with that RAM. Entity classes are automatically resolved from the selected RAM; arbitrary active entities (A) or objects (E) are not valid scheduler inputs.

questions.stem: When this property is set to true, Risk, Entity, and Risk Statement forms are impacted.

options.text: Migrate to Advanced Risk Assessments property

questions.explanation: The "Migrate to Advanced Risk Assessments" property replaces the legacy risk lifecycle on the Risk form with the Assessment Summary section and impacts the Risk, Entity, and Risk Statement forms. It is found at Advanced Risk Assessment > Administration > Properties and is not enabled by default.

questions.stem: Which table stores the links from Control Objective to Citation?
questions.explanation: sn_compliance_m2m_statement_citation (A). Option B (sn_compliance_m2m_policy_statement) links Policy to Control Objective. Option C is an inverse naming. Option D (sn_compliance_m2m_policy_profile_type) links Policy to Entity Type. The table name in option A has a typo ("cftation") but correctly identifies the relationship.

questions.stem: The Single Loss Expectancy is $1.000.000 and the Annual Rate of Occurrence is 20%. What is the Annualized Loss Expectancy?
questions.explanation: ALE (Annualized Loss Expectancy) = SLE x ARO. With SLE = $1,000,000 and ARO = 20% (0.20): ALE = $1,000,000 x 0.20 = $200,000. Options A ($1M) ignores the ARO factor; C ($2M) incorrectly doubles the SLE; D ($10K) applies no valid formula.

questions.stem: What options are available when configuring the assessment context for a risk assessment methodology RAM)? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: When configuring the assessment context for a RAM, the two available options are Risk (C) — assessing individual Risk records — and Object (D) — assessing records from any designated ServiceNow table. Risk Statement (A), Application Risk (B), and Project Risk (E) are not valid assessment context options for a RAM.

questions.stem: What are key prerequisites for a control test task to be generated?

options.text: Entity being scoped has associated controls with test plans
Entity being scoped has associated risks

questions.explanation: A control test task is generated when an engagement moves to the Validate or Fieldwork state, but only for entities that have associated controls with test plans. The entity must have controls scoped to the engagement and those controls must have test plans defined. Without test plans (C), no control test tasks are created.

questions.stem: Who should be directly involved in GRC implementations? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: ServiceNow platform experts (C) who configure and deploy the application; risk and compliance domain experts (E) who define the GRC programme requirements; and the CMDB process owner (F) who ensures entity data from CMDB is accurate and available. Board (A), CEO (B), and HR analysts (D) are not typically direct implementation participants.

questions.stem: Creating Entities in ServiceNow is easier as customers can leverage existing data used in other applications. What are some baseline tables that are commonly used to build an Entity Type? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The most commonly used ServiceNow baseline tables for building Entity Types are cmn_location (A), which represents physical and logical locations, and core_company (B), which represents organisations and business units. These are the most widely adopted tables because GRC scoping often follows an organisation's geographic and corporate structure. cmn_department (C) is also used but less foundational.

questions.stem: What types of tasks are specific to the Audit module? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Audit-specific task types are Interview (B), Walkthrough (C), and Control Test (D), all confirmed in the scheduled jobs table and task creation documentation. Control Attestation (A) is a compliance task. Tabletop Exercise (E) belongs to Business Continuity Management. Remediation (F) is an issue management task.

questions.stem: Which Script include can be modified to change how the compliance scores roll up?
questions.explanation: The ComplianceScoreCalculator script include governs how compliance scores are aggregated and rolled up across controls, entities, and the compliance hierarchy in ServiceNow GRC. Modifying this script include is the supported approach for customising score rollup logic to match customer-specific requirements.

questions.stem: What are primary tables for the GRC Advanced Risk application scope? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Primary tables for the GRC Advanced Risk application scope include sn_risk_advanced_risk_assessment_methodology (A, with typo in question) and sn_risk_advanced_factor (E). sn_risk_response_task (C) belongs to the GRC Risk scope, not the Advanced Risk scope. Options B and D are not primary Advanced Risk tables.

questions.stem: Controls are automatically moved to which state from the attestation phase?
questions.explanation: The documentation explicitly states "Controls are automatically moved to Review from the attestation phase." This is part of the standard control lifecycle: Attest -> Review. Monitor (D) is a subsequent state that is set manually; the automatic transition from attestation is specifically to Review (B).

questions.stem: EMEA Data Centers are an example of what?
questions.explanation: "EMEA Data Centers" represents a grouping or category of data center records filtered by region. In ServiceNow GRC, this corresponds to an Entity Type — a configuration that uses an Entity Filter to dynamically identify all matching records (individual data center CIs) as Entities. The Entity Type defines what EMEA Data Centers are; the individual data centers would be the Entities.

questions.stem: What is the minimum role required to approve a Policy?
questions.explanation: The policy approver is responsible for reviewing and approving policies in the Awaiting Approval state. In ServiceNow, the minimum role required to act on a policy approval is sn_compliance.user (C). The user must also be designated as an approver on the specific policy form to receive the approval task.

questions.stem: Which roles can move the control to the ‘Monitor’ state manually? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Moving a Control record to the Monitor state requires either the System Administrator role (D), which has platform-wide authority, or the Compliance Manager role (E), which governs the full control lifecycle. Compliance Reader (A) is read-only; Risk User (B) and Audit User (C) do not govern compliance control state transitions.

questions.stem: All of the following are tables which exist within the GRC Profiles application scope EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Risk Management application scope, not the GRC Profiles scope.

questions.stem: The compliance score calculation may be modified by changing which control factor?
questions.explanation: The compliance score calculation can be modified by changing the Control Weight (D) factor — it assigns relative importance to individual controls when calculating overall compliance scores. Higher-weighted controls have more impact on the final score. Control Height (A), Mass (B), and Velocity (C) are not valid GRC configuration terms.

questions.stem: Which of the following tables are included in the GRC: Policy and Compliance Management scoped application? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Policy and Compliance scoped application (sn_compliance_ prefix) contains: Policy [sn_compliance_policy] (B), Control Objective/Policy Statement [sn_compliance_policy_statement] (D), and Citation [sn_compliance_citation] (G). sn_grc_ prefix tables (C, E, F) belong to GRC Common/Profiles scope. sn_compliance_risk (A) is not a standard table.

questions.stem: What is the Risk likelihood called when using the Quantitative method?
questions.explanation: Annualized Rate of Occurrence (ARO) (D) is the quantitative likelihood measure — defines "Inherent ARO: Probability that a risk occurs in any given year before any mitigation strategies are in place." ALE = SLE x ARO, where SLE is monetary impact. Qualitative risk uses an ordinal Likelihood scale; ARO is its quantitative equivalent.

questions.stem: Which tables in the GRC: Profiles scope are parent tables for GRC: Risk Management tables? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: GRC Profiles scope parent tables that Risk Management tables extend from: Item [sn_grc_item] (A) — Risk/Control extend Item; Content [sn_grc_content] (C) — Risk Statement extends Content; Document [sn_grc_document] (E) — Risk Framework extends Document. Profile (D) is an entity instance table. Task (B) is a base platform table outside Profiles scope.

questions.stem: How can a user respond to consolidated (grouped) attestations? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create subgroups for responding with same or different responses
Provide response using a baseline template for grouped attestations
Provide different responses for each assessment
Provide same response for all assessments
Provide entity class responses within the same grouping

questions.explanation: Consolidated (grouped) attestations allow respondents to provide the same response for all assessments in the group (D) or provide different responses for each individual assessment (C). Both options are available in one UI. Subgroups (A), baseline templates (B), and entity class responses (E) are not valid consolidated attestation options.

questions.stem: Why is Entity scoping important when implementing GRC? (Choose three.)

options.text: Auto-generates controls when control objective is scoped with entity type
Provides a consistent approach to setting up risks and controls
Allows identification of both a technical owner and a business owner
Dynamic in nature. As new records meet criteria, they will be added as entities
Provides a consistent approach to issue tracking
