questions.explanation: Entity scoping is important because: it auto-generates controls when control objectives are scoped with entity types (A), provides a consistent approach to setting up risks and controls (B), and is dynamic — new records meeting criteria are automatically added as entities (D). Owner identification (C) and issue tracking approach (E) are not primary entity scoping benefits.

questions.stem: Why would a company need to comply with the General Data Protection Regulation?

options.text: It faces the most pervasive cyber-threats
It processes data from individuals in the European Union
It is publicly traded in the United States

questions.explanation: GDPR applies to organizations that process personal data of individuals in the European Union (C). It is not triggered by credit card storage (A — that is PCI DSS), cyber-threat exposure (B), or US stock exchange listing (D — that is SOX/SEC). GDPR was enacted May 25, 2018 to protect EU citizen data rights.

questions.stem: What is a risk register?
questions.explanation: A risk register is a repository of all identified risks (D), storing key attributes such as name, description, owner, frequency, inherent/residual levels, business impact, and mitigation plans. The risk register is the central repository for known and potential risks — not unidentified risks (A), frameworks (B), assessments (C), or criteria (E).

questions.stem: Which tables store the links from the Entity Types to Policies and Entity Types to Control Objectives? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Two m2m tables store Entity Type links: sn_compliance_m2m_policy_profile_type (B) links Entity Types to Policies; sn_compliance_m2m_statement_profile_type (C) links Entity Types to Control Objectives. Option A (policy_profile) stores entity-to-policy links. Option D is a risk-specific m2m table. Both B and C have the _profile_type suffix indicating Entity Type relationships.

questions.stem: Control Objectives are not active until the parent policy is in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Control Objectives are not active — cannot generate controls or be assessed — until the parent Policy reaches Published (C) state. In Draft (B), Review (D), and Awaiting Approval (A) states, control objectives exist but are inactive for compliance monitoring purposes.

questions.stem: What tables can leverage the SLA definition n the baseline? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Issue [sn_grc_issue] (B), which extends Task and has resolution SLAs, and Indicator Task [sn_grc_indicator_task] (C), which also extends Task and has completion SLAs. Risk (A), Control (D), and Control Objective (E) do not extend the Task table and cannot leverage baseline SLA definitions.

questions.stem: Which tables extend from the Task table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Tables extending from Task [task]: Risk Response Task [sn_risk_response_task] (A) and RCM Action Task [sn_risk_action_task] (D). Risk [sn_risk_risk] (B) and Control [sn_compliance_control] (C) extend Item [sn_grc_item]. Risk Statement [sn_risk_definition] (E) extends Content [sn_grc_content]. Task-extending tables relate to workflow actions, not core GRC objects.

questions.stem: The compliance or non-compliance of a control impacts the compliance score on records in which tables? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: A control's compliance status rolls up through the GRC hierarchy, impacting the Citation score (F), which rolls up to Policy (E) and then Authority Document (D). Audit Engagement (A) uses separate audit scoring; Risk (B) and Risk Statement (C) have independent quantitative/qualitative scoring separate from control compliance.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a type of compliance indicator?
questions.explanation: Valid compliance indicator types are Manual (B), Basic (E), Scripted (C), and Performance Analytics (A). "Reference" (D) is not a defined indicator type in ServiceNow GRC. Basic uses automated filter conditions; Scripted uses custom scripts; Performance Analytics uses PA data sources; Manual uses assigned tasks.

questions.stem: The content table (sn_grc_content) is a parent table of:
questions.explanation: sn_grc_content is the parent table for Content-type GRC records including Citations, Control Objectives, and Risk Statements (sn_risk_statement / sn_risk_defmition). sn_risk_framework (A) extends Document; sn_grc_profile (B) is the Entity table; sn_risk_risk (D) extends Item — none extend the Content base table.

questions.stem: Which tables extend from the Task table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Policy [sn_compliance_policy] (D) and Authority Document [sn_compliance_authority_document] (B) both extend the Document [sn_grc_document] base table, which extends the Task [task] table for workflow capabilities. Control Objective (A) and Citation (C) extend Content [sn_grc_content], which does not extend Task — distinguishing Document-type from Content-type GRC records.

questions.stem: What is the maximum file size that can be uploaded to OneDrive for policy authoring?
questions.explanation: The maximum file size for OneDrive policy authoring is 4 MB (B). Google Drive has a 10 MB limit. Option C (5 MB) is the ZIP file size limit for TPRM package uploads, not OneDrive policy authoring. Options A (no limit) and D (6 MB) do not correspond to any documented OneDrive limit.

questions.stem: Where does a user configure the Impact Assessment record?

options.text: Impact Assessment Flow in Flow Designer

questions.explanation: Impact Assessment records are configured using Regulatory Change Assessment Templates (B), which define the methodology for assessing the impact of regulatory changes. Option A (Flow Designer) handles automation workflows, C (Risk Assessment Methodologies) is for risk RAMs, and D (Risk Assessment Templates) is for risk assessments.

questions.stem: What is associated with the control objective, that is active with the setting to create controls automatically enabled, to generate controls?
questions.explanation: When "Creates controls automatically" is enabled on a control objective, associating an Entity Type (B) triggers automatic control generation — one control per entity of that type. Citations (A), indicator templates (C), and policies (D) are not the association that triggers automatic control creation.

questions.stem: What table is an implementer’s starting point to meet a customer requirement to generate a report related to a specific policy acknowledgement campaign?
questions.explanation: The Policy Acknowledgement Campaign table [sn_compliance_policy_acknowledgement] (C) is the implementer starting point for campaign reports — it contains all campaign metadata, audience definitions, and aggregate results. The Instance table (A) stores individual respondent responses. Audience (B) is a configuration table. Policy (D) is the parent record, not campaign-specific.

questions.stem: What tables are a part of the GRC: Advanced Risk scope? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: GRC: Advanced Risk scope includes Manual Factor (B) — customer-defined factors for assessing risks in a RAM — and Risk Assessment Methodologies (D) — the RAM records themselves. Risk Framework (A) and Risk Criteria Matrix (C) are components of classic GRC: Risk Management scope, not the Advanced Risk scoped application.

questions.stem: What choices do implementers have when configuring an audience for policy acknowledgements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Define conditions against the User table
Define conditions against the Group table

questions.explanation: Audience configuration options are: select specific individual users (A), define conditions against the User table via User Filters (B), and select specific predefined groups (C). The three tabs are Users, Groups, and User Filters. ACLs (D), Group table conditions (E), and User Criteria (F) are not standard audience configuration methods.

questions.stem: What rules can be set up to manage policy exceptions? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Two rule types govern the exception process: Verification rules (B) gate who verifies the request, and Approval rules (E) define multi-level approval flows. Alert (A), Entity class (C), Initial Approval (D), and Notification (F) are not defined rule types in the GRC Approval Configurator for policy exceptions.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow applications outside of the GRC suite of applications provide indicator templates when activated? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: ServiceNow applications outside GRC providing indicator templates when activated are Event Management (A) and Vulnerability Response (C). These integrations extend GRC monitoring with event-based and vulnerability indicators respectively. Customer Service Management (B), Configuration Compliance (D), and Security Incident Response (E) do not provide GRC indicator templates on activation.

questions.stem: What is the technical name of the table that contains entities?
questions.explanation: The Entity table (renamed from Profile in prior releases) has the technical name sn_grc_profile(s) (B), in the GRC: Profiles (sn_grc) application scope. sn_compliance_entities (A) and sn_grc_entities (C) do not exist. sn_compliance_profiles (D) incorrectly combines the compliance scope prefix with the profile table suffix.

questions.stem: What are the primary records provided in the Technology Controls content pack?
questions.explanation: The Technology Controls Monitoring Accelerator content pack provides Indicator templates (C) as its primary records — 273 templates for CIS v7 (94 Basic, 174 Manual, 5 Scripted) plus 67 for CIS v8. Assessment templates (A), PA indicator templates (B), and test plan templates (D) are not the primary content type delivered by this accelerator.

questions.stem: What must an implementer configure to allow users to submit a policy exception from a non-GRC application like HR? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Enabling exceptions from a non-GRC application (e.g. HR) requires: Integration Registry (A) to map the non-GRC source table, and an Exception questionnaire (D) for the request form. Approval rules (B), risk rules (C), and verification rules (E) are optional GRC-internal configurations not required for non-GRC integration.

questions.stem: If an implementer wanted to roll-up the quantitative values for a risk assessment methodology, what field would they update on the RAM?
questions.explanation: To roll up quantitative ALE values, the implementer updates the "Calculate ALE based on" field (C) on the RAM, designating which source record column stores the residual ALE result after assessment. This field only appears when Assessment contribution is Quantitative or Both. Options A and D are not valid RAM fields; B governs qualitative score calculation.

questions.stem: What actions can be executed by a user with the GRC Business User Lite role? (Choose two.)

options.text: Respond to GRC issues assigned to them

questions.explanation: GRC Business User Lite can respond to GRC issues assigned to them (B) and take/respond to a risk assessment (E). They cannot group control attestations (A — requires full business_user), approve advanced risk assessments (C — separate role configuration required), or create risk assessments (D — restricted to higher roles).

questions.stem: Which indicator type uses platform automation to collect records for continuous monitoring?
questions.explanation: Basic indicators (D) use platform automation — an indicator source specifying a table and collection frequency — to automatically collect records for continuous monitoring. Scripted indicators (B) use custom scripts. Manual indicators (A) use assigned tasks. "Automatic" (C) is not a valid indicator type; the automated type is called Basic.

questions.stem: What feature does the GRC: Advanced Risk application have that is not available in the GRC: Risk Management (Classic Risk) application?
questions.explanation: Risk score rollup (C) is exclusive to Advanced Risk — scores are aggregated across risk statement hierarchy and entity hierarchy to provide rolled-up risk posture visibility. Classic Risk does not support score rollup/aggregation. Risk indicator management (A), risk response (B), and risk score tracking (D) exist in both classic and advanced risk.

questions.stem: What tables can be related to the Control Objective table with a many-to-many relationship? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Control Objective has m2m relationships with: Citation (C) — via Content Reference to Control Objective [sn_grc_m2m_cont_ref_ps]; and Policy (E) — a control objective can belong to multiple policies and vice versa. Authority Document (A) relates via Citations, not directly. Control (B) and Risk (D) have direct (not m2m) relationships to Control Objectives.

questions.stem: What is located in the GRC Properties module under the Policy and Compliance application menu?

options.text: System Properties for GRC: Entities scope
System Properties for all GRC application scopes
System Properties for the GRC: Profiles scope
System Properties for the GRC: Policy and Compliance scope

questions.explanation: The GRC Properties module under the Policy and Compliance menu exposes System Properties for the GRC: Profiles (sn_grc) application scope (C). Option D (Policy and Compliance scope) is incorrect. Options A (Entities scope) and B (all GRC scopes) do not accurately describe the module's scope.

questions.stem: How can common controls be generated?

options.text: Create a common control as a child of a control objective
Create a common control as a child of a standard control

questions.explanation: Common controls are generated by converting an existing standard control (B) using the "Convert to Common" UI action. There is no direct creation or auto-generation path for common controls. Options A and D (child records) are not valid approaches. Option C (direct creation) is explicitly excluded by documentation.

questions.stem: What happens to the standard control if it is selected to become a reliant entity on a common control?

options.text: Standard control state changes to Converted
Standard control state changes to Retired
Standard control continues in its current state

questions.explanation: When a standard control is selected as a reliant entity on a common control, the standard control's state changes to Retired (C). The common control inherits responsibility for testing. The standard control is not deleted (A). "Converted" (B) is not a valid control state. Option D (no change) is incorrect.

questions.stem: What state do controls enter once all control attestations are completed?
questions.explanation: Doc The docs state controls in the Review state are automatically moved there — confirming Review (A) is the automatic next state once all control attestations are completed. After the compliance manager reviews results in Review, controls advance to Monitor for ongoing monitoring. Lifecycle: Draft -> Attest -> Review -> Monitor -> Retired.

questions.stem: What persona approves the release of the content for auditors outside the organization?
questions.explanation: The Audit Approver [sn_audit.approver] (C) is the persona who approves engagements and audit plans, including formal approval to release audit content to external auditors. Audit Admin (A) manages application configuration; Audit Process Owner (B) is a functional stakeholder; Audit Engagement Project Manager (D) manages execution, not formal release approval.

questions.stem: What is the minimum role required to create a new RAM?
questions.explanation: Creating a Risk Assessment Methodology requires the Advanced Risk Assessment Admin [sn_risk_advanced.ara_admin] role (E), as RAM creation is an administrative configuration task. ara_assessor (A) is for taking assessments; sn_risk.manager (B) governs standard risk; sn_risk.user (C) is read/participate; ara_creator (D) is not a valid Advanced Risk role name.

questions.stem: What circumstances will cause the Rollup Configuration options to only appear on a risk assessment methodology?
questions.explanation: Rollup Configuration options appear on a RAM only when Assessment Context is set to Risk (A). This context assesses an entity and its related risk statements, requiring score propagation through a rollup hierarchy. Object context (D) assesses arbitrary records without rollup; Entity (B) and blank (C) are not valid Assessment Context values.

questions.stem: What happens if an entity is set to auto-update the owner value from the source record and the value on the source record field has been cleared?

options.text: The entity owner will be cleared
The entity owner will become the same as the control objective owner
Nothing, the entity owner will remain
The entity owner will become the default owner defined in the entity filter

questions.explanation: When auto-update is enabled but the source record owner field is cleared, the entity owner remains unchanged (C). The auto-update only pushes non-empty values; a cleared source field does not clear the entity owner. The Default owner field on the entity filter ensures every entity always retains an owner. Options A, B, and D do not reflect the documented behaviour.

questions.stem: What must an implementer configure to allow users to submit a policy exception from a GRC application?
questions.explanation: From within a GRC application, users can submit policy exceptions without any additional configuration (B) — the built-in exception workflow is natively available. Integration Registry (A) and Exception questionnaire (D) are only required when integrating non-GRC applications with the exception process.

questions.stem: What risk appetite definitions are configurable versus customizable?
questions.explanation: Appetite scales (A) are configurable — administrators define and map qualitative appetite scales to risk rating criteria to calculate appetite status. Tolerance scales (B) are derived from appetite scales. Appetite status (C) and Tolerance status (E) are calculated outputs, not user-configured definitions. Appetite roles (D) is not a risk appetite concept.

questions.stem: What is the overall goal of entity classes?

options.text: To provide specific information about an Entity, such as who owns the Entity
Slow relationships between Entities and policies and map them directly to Citations
To enable reporting and to support advance risk assessment
Associate Control Objectives and Risk Statements with Risks and Controls

questions.explanation: Entity classes serve two primary purposes — enabling hierarchical reporting (grouping entities for dashboards and metrics) and supporting advanced risk assessment (RAM applicability and risk appetite are defined per entity class) (C). Entity ownership (A) is an entity record attribute, not the purpose of entity classes. Option D describes GRC item-to-content relationships.

questions.stem: In the Technology Controls content pack, some of the indicator templates are related to the ISO 27002 regulation. What field connects the indicator templates to the regulation?
questions.explanation: Indicator templates in the Technology Controls content pack are connected to the ISO 27002 regulation via the Related source IDs (C) field, which stores cross-framework regulatory reference identifiers enabling multi-standard mapping. Options A and B reference non-existent field names; D (UCF Content Reference ID) maps to UCF content, not ISO 27002 specifically.

questions.stem: What is the prefix for tables in the Advanced Risk scope?
questions.explanation: All tables in the GRC: Advanced Risk application scope use the prefix sn_risk_advanced_ (A), e.g. sn_risk_advanced_risk_assessment_methodology and sn_risk_advanced_factor. The prefix sn_risk_ara_ (B) does not exist; sn_advanced_risk_ (C) and sn_ara_ (D) are not ServiceNow Advanced Risk table naming conventions.

questions.stem: What actions can be executed by a user with the GRC Business User role? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The GRC Business User role permits: taking risk assessments (A) when assigned as an assessor, and participating in group attestations (C). Business users have read access to policies and control objectives and can submit issues or exceptions. Grouping issues (B), creating policies (D), and creating risks (E) require manager or admin roles.

questions.stem: What templates are provided in the GRC: Technology Controls Monitoring Accelerator application?
questions.explanation: The GRC: Technology Controls Monitoring Accelerator delivers Indicator templates (D) as its primary pre-built content for automating cybersecurity control monitoring. Risk templates (A) belong to GRC: Risk Management; Metric templates (B) are not a GRC template type; Control test templates (C) belong to GRC: Audit Management.

questions.stem: Using the Risk Workspace, the Risk assessment planning section allows a user to generate RAM instances. What is the ServiceNow guided set up function used?
questions.explanation: The Risk assessment planning section uses a Playbook (A) — the Risk assessment scope playbook — to guide users through defining the RAM, scoping entities, and initiating assessments. Runbooks (B) are an IT Operations feature; Guidebook (C) and Now Assist (D) are not the guided workflow function for RAM instance generation.

questions.stem: What table can be related to the Policy table with a many-to-many relationship?
questions.explanation: The Policy table [sn_compliance_policy] is related to Control Objectives via the m2m table sn_compliance_m2m_policy_statement (E). Risk (A), Authority Document (B), Citation (C), and Control (D) are not directly related to Policy via an m2m relationship — they connect through other parts of the GRC content hierarchy.

questions.stem: What policy field defines who can perform the redlining function once the integration with Office 365 is configured for a customer?
questions.explanation: The Reviewer field (D) on the Policy record defines which users can perform the redlining function once Office 365/OneDrive integration is configured. Reviewers are designated policy collaborators with edit and mark-up access. Contributor (A), Knowledgebase Admin (B), and Acknowledgement Manager (C) do not govern redlining access.

questions.stem: What minimum role is required to use the Scheduled assessments module to generate RAM instances on the workspace?
questions.explanation: The minimum role to use the Scheduled Assessments module and generate RAM instances is Risk Manager [sn_risk.manager] (D). Risk Manager can schedule and initiate assessments. Risk User (A) can only participate; Risk Admin (B) has full access but is not the minimum; Sys Admin (C) has platform-wide access but is not the minimum GRC-specific role.

questions.stem: Which attribute is stored on the entity type record?
questions.explanation: The Compliance Score (B) field is stored on the Entity Type record, representing the aggregate compliance score calculated across all entities of that type. Entity Class (A) is a separate dimensional record; Entity Owner (C) and Auto-Update flag (D) are on the individual Entity record; Source (E) is an Entity record field, not an Entity Type attribute.

questions.stem: What record maintains the primary Risk Assessment Methodology that is displayed on the entity record?
questions.explanation: The Entity Class (D) record maintains the primary RAM displayed on the entity record, defining the applicable risk framework for groups of similarly classified entities. The Entity record (A) displays the RAM but does not define it; Entity Type (B) scopes GRC items; Entity Tier (C) is not a standard GRC term.

questions.stem: In the Technology Controls content pack, what citations are directly related to the indicator templates?
questions.explanation: The Technology Controls Monitoring Accelerator indicator templates are directly related to CIS Controls (A) — specifically CIS Controls v7.1 and v8 authority documents and their citations. ISO 27002 (B) links via Related source IDs; SOX (C) and COBIT (D) are not directly mapped as citation sources in this content pack.

questions.stem: What additional capabilities does the Advanced Audit application provide? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The Advanced Audit application adds Resource plans (B) and Cost plans (C) via PPM integration, creating an equivalent PPM project for each engagement. Observation management (A) is standard audit functionality; WBS structure (D) is not added by Advanced Audit; auto-generation of audit tasks (E) is a standard feature, not specific to Advanced Audit.

questions.stem: How are advanced risk assessment responses to a group factor turned into a score?

options.text: By Qualitative Transformation Criteria on the Group Factor
By Factor Contribution Criteria on the Group Factor
By Aggregation method on the Group Factor
By Factor Weights on the Group Factor

questions.explanation: Group factor assessment responses are converted to a score using the Qualitative Transformation Criteria (A) defined on the group factor, mapping response value ranges to score values. Factor Contribution Criteria (B) governs individual factor contribution; Aggregation method (C) and Factor Weights (D) are not the scoring transformation mechanism.

questions.stem: What is the name of the job that generates entities from the entity filters?
questions.explanation: The GRC Profile Generation scheduled job (D) generates entities from entity filters by scanning filter conditions and creating entity records from matching source table records. Despite the Zurich rename from "Profile" to "Entity", the scheduled job retains the legacy name. GRC Cleanup (A) removes stale records; GRC Entity/Item Generation (B, C) are not valid job names.

questions.stem: What attributes can be set on an indicator template? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Indicator templates support Sample size (E), defining how many records are evaluated per execution, and Supporting data fields (F), specifying additional data collected with each indicator run. Tracking options (A), Virtualization options (B), User Criteria (C), and Alert rules (D) are not configurable attributes on indicator templates.
